title: India women's team refuses to take Asia Cup trophy from Mohsin Naqvi
content: India captain Harmanpreet Kaur and her teammates were seen celebrating after their record-extending eighth Women's Asia Cup title. However, the Indian team did not collect the trophy from Naqvi during the presentation ceremony. The ceremony ended with Sri Lanka receiving their runners-up cheque, medals and mementoes from the officials.

title: Oil infra hit by Ukraine, Russia gets 70% of its fuel from India
content: August marked a milestone for Russia as it imported record levels of oil products, with Indian exports accounting for nearly seventy percent. The gasoline supplied by India was produced from Russian crude at a shared refinery. While India remains the second-largest importer of crude oil from Russia, its overall imports have seen a decline compared to recent months, with China still leading the ranks.

title: Mark Zuckerberg's secret project wanted Meta teams 60% smaller and run by AI agents
content: Mark Zuckerberg ran a secret plan called Project OT to make Meta "AI native", with executives studying scenarios that cut some team sizes by up to 60%. The Meta layoffs of May 2026 removed 8,000 jobs, but a second November wave was scrapped after employee protests over keystroke tracking and weak AI productivity data. Meta is now asking Applied AI staff to become managers again, reversing its flatter structure push.

title: Israel released 28 wild donkeys in desert; 44 years later, they created an oasis
content: In an effort to rejuvenate the parched landscape of Israel's Ramon Crater, wild donkeys were brought back into the ecosystem. These resilient animals played a crucial role by creating waterholes, which became essential for desert wildlife. Additionally, their droppings helped spread acacia seeds, promoting the growth of trees. Their natural movements resulted in water-retaining depressions, significantly transforming the area's ecology into a thriving environment that has caught global attention.

title: Anthropic researcher says humanity's future decided on 'MacBooks of engineers'
content: Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon has quit the AI industry, saying OpenAI and Anthropic are racing to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives. His post, now past 155 million views, has pulled two more AI safety researchers out of Anthropic and Google and drawn a pacing plan from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, backed by Sam Altman and Elon Musk. Anthropic alignment lead Evan Hubinger puts the odds AI kills everyone above 10 per cent.

title: How Travis Kelce turned his $3.13M rookie deal into a business empire
content: Travis Kelce has successfully diversified his interests beyond the football field. Co-owning Garage Beer and investing in Casa Azul Tequila Soda are just the start. Collaborating with Jana Partners for a stake in Six Flags and joining an investment group for the Alpine Formula One team highlights his ambition, as he focuses on aligning his ventures with his personal passions while aligning them with opportunities to grow his brand.

title: How Trinity Rodman escaped Dennis Rodman’s shadow to build her own legacy
content: Trinity Rodman’s journey goes far beyond soccer. As a child, she lived with her mother and brother in a car and motels during a difficult period. Her mother, Michelle Moyer, became her biggest support and role model. Today, Trinity is an Olympic champion, NWSL champion and the league’s highest-paid player, after building her career on her own terms.

title: The Uranium rush: Inside India's scramble to fuel its nuclear ambitions
content: India is securing uranium fuel for its ambitious nuclear expansion program.  Uzbekistan, Australia, and Canada are key partners in this global fuel hunt.  New domestic laws allow private companies to build nuclear power plants.  This move creates significant demand for uranium fuel supplies.  India's long-term strategy also involves developing thorium resources.

title: A year on, Rs 15 lakh for kin of 4 killed in Leh firing
content: Ladakh's Lieutenant Governor announced compensation for four protesters killed last September.  An ex gratia of Rs 3 lakh for major injuries and Rs 1 lakh for minor injuries was also approved.  This follows demonstrations demanding statehood and constitutional safeguards under Schedule Six.  Authorities imposed restrictions and arrested over eighty people after the violent protests occurred.  Cases against those arrested will be withdrawn and victims will receive compensation.

title: India avenge 2024 final defeat, beat Sri Lanka to lift 8th Asia Cup title
content: In an exhilarating final, India Women clinched the Women's T20 Asia Cup title by overcoming Sri Lanka. Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana stood out, crafting a robust opening partnership that propelled India’s score. The bowlers shone, especially Shree Charani, who captured four wickets and effectively dismantled Sri Lanka's batting lineup, securing India's remarkable eighth victory in this prestigious tournament.

title: Abhishek, Arshdeep shine as India beat Afghanistan by 7 wickets in 1st T20I
content: India dominated the first T20I, achieving a decisive seven-wicket victory over Afghanistan. The highlight was Abhishek Sharma, whose explosive 82 runs from 32 balls led the charge against a target of 156 set by Afghanistan, despite their recovery efforts from Omarzai and Nabi. On the bowling side, Arshdeep Singh excelled with 3 wickets for just 19 runs, allowing India to take a lead of 1-0 in this thrilling three-match series.

title: Stock market holiday: Are NSE, BSE closed for trading on Ganesh Chaturthi?
content: On September 14, stock markets will halt trading in observance of Ganesh Chaturthi. While equity derivatives will remain suspended for the day, the commodity market will only partially close during the morning session. Trading will pick back up in the evening session. Investors should keep these adjustments in mind as they plan their trading activities around the festival.

title: Woman loses 70 kilos to donate kidney to husband, then gives it to a stranger
content: Rinat Kara embarked on a remarkable journey to lose seventy kilograms in order to donate a kidney to her husband, Meir, who faced severe complications from diabetes. Through a paired exchange program, Rinat's kidney was given to a stranger, while Meir received a compatible organ, enabling him to end dialysis. This inspiring act sheds light on the profound importance of organ donation and the serious challenges posed by diabetes.

title: Quote of the day by Judi Dench
content: Judi Dench expresses a profound belief in confronting harsh realities rather than seeking comfort. This notion, explored through her character in 'Notes on a Scandal', reflects a timeless understanding of human behavior. Dench’s remarkable journey from her humble beginnings and diverse stage presence to notable film roles, such as those in James Bond, has solidified her as a cinematic powerhouse.

title: Masked men open fire at Punjabi singer Gulab Sidhu’s residence; CCTV video emerges
content: In a shocking incident, gunfire erupted at the residence of Punjabi singer Gulab Sidhu in Barnala district, as captured by CCTV footage. This occurrence, which took place early Sunday morning while Sidhu was out of the country, raises serious concerns for his safety. Notably, he has faced threats before, including those from a village sarpanch, prompting police to assign him security personnel. Investigations into the shooting are ongoing.

title: 75 students fall sick with vomiting, diarrhoea at Surat boarding school
content: At least seventy-five students fell sick with suspected food poisoning at a Surat boarding school. Twelve students required hospitalization after developing symptoms like diarrhoea and vomiting. Four students have since been discharged, while others remain in stable condition. Health officials inspected the school hostel and collected food samples for testing. A mobile medical team is also conducting health check-ups of all students.

title: 3-year-old’s ‘asthma’ cough was a warning sign of a fatal heart condition
content: A young girl's persistent cough led to the discovery of a serious heart condition. Doctors advise parents to seek evaluation for prolonged coughs and fatigue. Heart issues can mimic respiratory problems, requiring careful medical assessment. Clinical examinations and tests like echocardiograms help identify cardiac concerns. Awareness of subtle symptoms can prompt timely medical consultations for children.

title: 51 wides! Arshdeep Singh creates big unwanted record in India vs Afghanistan 1st T20I
content: Arshdeep Singh's 51 wides accounted for 7.4% of all the balls he bowled during the period. Renegades' R Ngarava and West Indies' Jason Holder follow with 38 wides each, while New Zealand's Jacob Duffy and West Indies' Romario Shepherd have bowled 36 each.

title: Fed, crude, dollar and Iran war: 4 factors that could move gold next week
content: Gold and silver prices are expected to remain volatile next week. The US Federal Reserve's interest rate decision will be a key global event. Crude oil movements and the US dollar will also influence market sentiment. Other central banks' monetary policy and inflation data will be closely watched. Geopolitical developments and economic data will drive precious metals' direction.

title: After IND vs AFG first, ‘Vande Mataram’ set to become regular before India matches
content: The national song Vande Mataram was sung before the India vs Afghanistan cricket match on Sunday. Parliament had recently passed a bill making insults to the national song a punishable offense. The full six-stanza version of Vande Mataram was sung during the recent match. This amendment extends legal protection to the national song, similar to the national anthem.

title: Happy Ganesh Chaturthi 2026: Wishes, messages, quotes and status
content: As Ganesh Chaturthi approaches, families engage in a thorough cleaning and prepare their homes for the joyous celebration. This festival is not only about welcoming Bappa but also about uniting in prayers and fostering a sense of community. It embodies messages of faith, gratitude, and hope for the future. A variety of greetings, statuses, and captions are available for sharing festive cheer and blessings for the coming year.

title: Mecca Pact, but no troops yet: Pak expresses 'solidarity' with Saudi after Houthi attacks
content: Pakistan voiced strong solidarity with Saudi Arabia following recent Houthi attacks.  These strikes threaten regional peace and could disrupt global energy supplies.  Prime Minister Sharif discussed these issues with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.  The recent Houthi advances have also intensified concerns over Red Sea shipping routes.  A mutual-defense pact between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye is now under renewed focus.

title: 7 addl cops, 37 DCPs, 16,000+ personnel: How Mumbai Police are securing Ganeshotsav
content: Mumbai Police have deployed over sixteen thousand personnel for Ganeshotsav celebrations.  This extensive security includes numerous officers and specialized units across the city.  Additional forces will be present for the Ganesh idol immersion day.  Citizens are urged to cooperate with security and report suspicious objects.  Immediate police assistance is available by contacting the helpline numbers.

title: Scissors, screwdriver on bed: Man killed ‘lover’ in Assam hotel
content: A woman was discovered deceased in a Rangia hotel room with throat injuries. Police arrested a man who had booked the room and was found inside. The victim was identified as Malini Guria from Sonitpur district. Preliminary inquiry suggests the crime may be linked to a love affair. The accused has confessed to the murder before the police.

title: Inside Martha Stewart’s 152-acre New York farm with 100 chickens
content: Martha Stewart bought a 152-acre farmhouse in Katonah, new york, in 2000 . it became a working farm, creative laboratory and carefully managed home for an ever-growing collection of animals . over the next 26 years, the property evolved into Bedford Farm, also known as Cantitoe Corners, with horses, gardens, historic and modern buildings .

title: Chinese FM Wang Yi stepped in for Xi at PM Modi’s Brics gala dinner: Reports
content: foreign minister Wang Yi represented china at the dinner . the reason for Xi’s absence was not immediately known . a source suggested that the Chinese president had returned to his hotel to rest . sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed, who had attended the summit earlier in the day, was among the notable absentees .

title: Mayawati refutes illness claims, appears before media to dispel doubts
content: mayawati says she is well and what all is being said about her health are rumours . she cited a late-night call to her office by nephew Akash Anand as evidence that such claims were being circulated . the former party president said she was fine and engaged in party work .

title: ‘Some regional countries requested’: Iran after meeting with Gulf states in Oman postponed
content: the meeting was to discuss a range of issues, including possible agreements on the Strait of Hormuz . it was a joint decision between Tehran and Muscat . a meeting between Iran and Gulf states scheduled for Monday in Oman was postponed .

title: Brics 2026: Xi listening, PM Modi warns against weaponisation of minerals, tech
content: the remarks mirrored Modi’s exhortation for Brics at the Rio summit last year to work towards secure and reliable supply chains . the remarks amplified global concerns about the politically fraught issue of China’s near monopoly over critical minerals processing, while also cutting towards the West for its tendency to use technology as a means of political exclusion .

title: Murder accused's 'victory march': SC asks Haryana police to produce him in court

title: Sweden opposition holds slender lead in tight election, projection shows a
